# Introduction

`iseeSpatial` adds spatial panels to `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("iSEE")` for data at
cellular resolution: imaging-based (CosMx, Xenium) and sequencing-based
(Visium HD, cell-segmented). A region selected on an overview map is applied
to every panel, and analyses (spatial statistics, spatially variable genes,
niches, domains) run on that region.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("iseeSpatial")
```

# A small example

We simulate a tissue with two zones so the vignette runs without downloads.

```{r simulate}
library(iseeSpatial)
set.seed(1)
n <- 2000
xy <- cbind(x = runif(n, 0, 1000), y = runif(n, 0, 1000))
zone <- ifelse(xy[, "x"] < 500, "left", "right")
type <- ifelse(zone == "left",
               sample(c("Tumor", "T.cells"), n, TRUE, c(0.8, 0.2)),
               sample(c("Fibroblast", "T.cells"), n, TRUE, c(0.7, 0.3)))
counts <- matrix(rpois(30 * n, 2), 30, n,
                 dimnames = list(paste0("GENE", 1:30), paste0("cell", 1:n)))
counts["GENE1", zone == "left"] <- counts["GENE1", zone == "left"] + 5
spe <- SpatialExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts, logcounts = log1p(counts)),
                         colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(Level1 = factor(type),
                                                        sum = colSums(counts)),
                         spatialCoords = xy)
spe <- setPlatform(spe, "visiumhd")
getPlatform(spe)
```

# Niches and spatial domains

The spatial neighbour graph is built once (k nearest cells) and stored on
the object. **k is a choice**, not a constant: small k describes direct
contacts, large k a wider region; pick it from the structures studied and
report it.

```{r niches}
spe <- buildSpatialGraph(spe, k = 15)
spe <- computeNiches(spe, label_col = "Level1", k = 15, n_niches = 3)
table(spe$niche)
summary(spe$niche_entropy)
```

Each cell's neighbourhood composition is kept, so one can ask, for example,
what surrounds tumour cells:

```{r composition}
comp <- reducedDim(spe, "NicheComposition")
round(colMeans(comp[spe$Level1 == "Tumor", ], na.rm = TRUE), 2)
```

Spatial domains cluster expression combined with the neighbourhood average
(`lambda` = weight of the neighbourhood; `lambda = 0` gives plain expression
clusters, returned as `expr_cluster` for comparison):

```{r domains}
reducedDim(spe, "PCA") <- prcomp(t(logcounts(spe)), rank. = 10)$x
spe <- computeSpatialDomains(spe, k_spatial = 15, lambda = 0.5, resolution = 0.5)
table(spe$spatial_domain, zone)
```

# Launching the app

```{r app}
app <- iseeSpatial(spe, mode = "analysis")
if (interactive()) shiny::runApp(app)
```

`mode = "qc"` gives a QC-oriented layout. Panels can also be combined with
any standard iSEE panel through `initial =`.

# Loading real data

```{r loaders, eval = FALSE}
spe <- load_cosmx("cos_isee_ready.RDS")               # prepared CosMx object
spe <- load_xenium("path/to/xenium_output")           # 10x Xenium bundle
spe <- load_visiumhd("path/to/segmented_outputs")     # 10x Visium HD, cell-segmented
```

The full Visium HD workflow of the OSTA book (QC, SingleR annotation), plus
niches and domains, is in
`system.file("scripts", "visiumhd_osta_workflow.R", package = "iseeSpatial")`.
